problems.problem: The plain sense goes outside the passage. 'famed as a horse-tamer' is not in the text. The Zhuangzi (9.6) has Poh Loh only claim that he understands the management of horses, and his fame comes from Giles' note ('A Chinese Rarey, of somewhat legendary character'). Rule 2 and the plan trap say a note is not the text.
problems.fix: Change the plain sense to 'Poh Loh, claiming to understand horses, sets to work;' and leave the reading as it is. It is the same length and entry-check comes back ok (scratch/critic3/f11.json).

problems.problem: Prose and rule 2. The plain sense's 'met an unsuited age' restates the key's own first clause ('If the age was unsuitable'), which is a paraphrase of the verse rather than context. It also doubles 'age' against the reading's 'a busy age' within one sentence.
problems.fix: Change the plain sense to 'The chapter says the retired scholars of old hid neither body, words nor wisdom;'. That is what 16.27 says just before the key, and it keeps the sentence at 45 words. Leave the reading unchanged. Entry-check comes back ok (scratch/critic3/f20.json).
